title: Reading the code symbols
intro: The code font joins some neighboring characters into a single visual symbol. Type the characters in the middle column, not a new symbol. This key includes only combinations that actually fuse in this book; their meaning still depends on the surrounding code. Commands, paths, comments and diffs appear alongside TypeScript.

meanings.!=: Loose inequality; the null check here also excludes undefined.
meanings.=>: An arrow function, or the return type in a function type.
meanings.&&: Logical AND; evaluates the right operand only when the left is truthy.
meanings.||: Logical OR; evaluates the right operand only when the left is falsy.
meanings.??: Nullish coalescing; uses the right operand when the left is null or undefined.
Optional chaining; stops this access when the receiver is null or undefined.
meanings.?:: The optional marker followed by the type annotation colon.
meanings.--: Decrement by one; also the prefix of long options in the printed commands.
Spread or rest syntax. In comments and strings, it can just mean omitted text.
The parent-directory component in the printed paths.
meanings.*/: Ends a block or documentation comment.
meanings.>>: Here, closes two nested type-argument lists.
meanings.>>>: Here, closes three nested type-argument lists.
meanings.>]: Adjacent closing delimiters: a type-argument list, then a bracket.
meanings.}}: Adjacent closing braces, including nested objects in the printed output.
meanings.__: Two underscores in an identifier; they have no special TypeScript meaning.
meanings.---: The old-file header in a printed diff.
meanings.+++: The new-file header in a printed diff.
